text:
Every Tuesday before noon, the box arrived. A cardboard cube, beaded with condensation from the ice packs inside, and she carried it to the kitchen counter. Parings knife, she slit the tape, sounded like a page tearing. Vacuum sealed chicken, kale, really old jade color, tiny vial of sesame oil. Recipe cards, printed, confident verbs, whisk, sear, drizzle. And the instructions, they assumed a second pair of hands. Someone to chop while she stirred, someone to laugh at the burnt garlic. She cooked anyway.
Browned the meat, lacquered in soy and honey, sprinkled scallions on the rice like green confetti. And the apartment filled with ginger and steam and, for twenty minutes, it felt less like she was passing through, more like home. Set two plates, habit she couldn't break. Then put one back in the cupboard before sitting down. It was good. It wasn't the same as cooking for someone who would ask for more.
After, washed the little plastic pouches, stacked them up, translucent postcards from a life she almost lived. The next recipe card, she put it on the fridge. Magnet, strawberry shaped. Promised lemon and thyme, bright, she didn't trust anymore, but she left it. So next week, Tuesday, another box. Every Tuesday, another box.
